p.src: After Jia Zheng returned to the capital and concluded all his official business, he was granted a month's leave to rest at home. As he was advancing in years, burdened with grave responsibilities, and declining in health, and as his several years away had separated him from his family, he now felt immeasurably happy and fortunate to be peacefully reunited with them at home. He put all affairs, great and small, still further out of mind and did nothing but read; when bored, he played chess and drank with his literary companions, or spent the daytime indoors with his mother, wife, and children, enjoying the intimate pleasures of family life. As the third day of the eighth month that year would mark Grandmother Jia's eightieth birthday, and all their relatives and friends were expected, there was concern that there would not be room to arrange all the banquets. Jia Zheng therefore consulted early with Jia She, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, and the others. They decided that from the twenty-eighth of the seventh month through the fifth of the eighth, banquets would be held simultaneously at the Rong and Ning mansions: the Ning mansion would entertain the male official guests, the Rong mansion the ladies, while spacious places in Prospect Garden, including Brocade Pavilion and Jiayin Hall, would be prepared as retiring rooms. On the twenty-eighth they would invite imperial kinsmen, imperial sons-in-law, princes and dukes, princesses, commandery princesses, princess consorts, noble ladies, and titled matrons; on the twenty-ninth, cabinet dignitaries, metropolitan and provincial commanders, and titled ladies; and on the thirtieth, senior officials and their titled wives, together with relatives, friends, and ladies from near and far. The first day of the eighth month was reserved for Jia She's family banquet, the second for Jia Zheng's, the third for Jia Zhen and Jia Lian's, and the fourth for a banquet jointly provided by every senior and junior member of the Jia clan. The fifth was jointly provided by the household stewards, including Lai Da and Lin Zhixiao. From early in the seventh month, bearers of birthday gifts arrived in an unending stream. By imperial command, the Ministry of Rites bestowed a gold-and-jade ruyi sceptre, four lengths of colored satin, four gold-and-jade rings, and five hundred taels of silver from the imperial treasury. Yuanchun also ordered eunuchs to deliver a golden God of Longevity, an aloeswood cane, a string of kalambac beads, a box of Felicity-and-Longevity incense, a pair of gold ingots, four pairs of silver ingots, twelve bolts of colored satin, and four jade cups. As for the rest, from princes and imperial sons-in-law down to the households of civil and military officials of every rank, none with whom the family had dealings failed to send a gift; they were too numerous to record. A large table was set up in the main hall and covered with red felt; all the finest gifts were displayed upon it for Grandmother Jia to inspect. For the first day or two Grandmother Jia happily came to look them over, but later she tired of it and would not inspect them, saying only, “Have Feng collect them. I shall look at them some other day when I am bored.” By the twenty-eighth, both mansions were hung with lanterns and decked in colored ornaments; screens painted with phoenixes stood open, cushions embroidered with lotus blossoms were laid out, and the music of pipes, flutes, drums, and strings carried across the main thoroughfares and through the side streets. At the Ning mansion that day there were only the Prince of Beijing, the Prince of Nan'an, the imperial son-in-law of Yongchang, the Prince of Leshan, and several hereditary dukes and marquises from families of long-standing friendship. At the Rong mansion were the Dowager Princess of Nan'an, the Princess of Beijing, and several titled wives of dukes and marquises from such families. Grandmother Jia and the others received them in full ceremonial dress appropriate to their ranks.

p.src: After exchanging greetings, the guests were first invited into Jiayin Hall in Prospect Garden. When they had taken tea and changed their clothes, they went to Rongqing Hall to offer birthday congratulations and take their seats at the banquet. After much polite yielding, they finally took their seats. The two upper tables were occupied by the princesses of Nan'an and Beijing; below them, in order of rank, sat the titled wives of the dukes and marquises. At the lower table on the left, the assisting hostesses were the titled wives of the Marquis of Jinxiang and the Earl of Linchang; Grandmother Jia's place as principal hostess was at the lower table on the right. Lady Xing and Lady Wang, accompanied by You-shi, Xifeng, and several daughters-in-law of the clan, stood in attendance behind Grandmother Jia in two spreading, wing-like rows. The wives of Lin Zhixiao and Lai Da directed the other married servants outside the bamboo blinds as they served food and wine, while Zhou Rui's wife led several maids who waited behind the folding screen to answer calls. The guests' attendants had already been taken elsewhere and entertained. Presently the actors performed their opening salutation onstage, while below it twelve young pages, all with their hair still unbound, stood uniformly in attendance. Soon a page carried the opera program to the foot of the steps and first handed it to the married servant charged with relaying messages. She received it and passed it to Lin Zhixiao's wife, who placed it on a small tea tray, slipped through the curtain, and handed it to Peifeng, You-shi's concubine. Only after Peifeng received it was it presented to You-shi. You-shi carried it to the upper tables. After politely declining for a while, the Dowager Princess of Nan'an selected an auspicious opera; following another round of courtesies, the Princess of Beijing also chose one. After everyone had exchanged further courtesies, they ordered the troupe simply to choose some good pieces and perform them. Before long, four courses had been presented and the first soup was served, while the attendants from the various households were given gratuities. Everyone then changed clothes and returned to the garden, where fine tea was served afresh.

p.src: When the Dowager Princess of Nan'an asked about Baoyu, Grandmother Jia replied with a smile, “The Sutra for Peace and Prolonged Life is being recited at several temples today, and he has gone to kneel through the services.” She then asked about the young ladies, and Grandmother Jia said with a smile, “Among the girls, some are ill and some delicate, and they are shy before strangers, so I had them stay behind to watch the house for me. Some young actors are available, so a troupe has been summoned to the hall over there, where they are watching a performance with their cousins from their aunts' families.” The Dowager Princess of Nan'an smiled. “If that is so, send someone to invite them here.” Grandmother Jia turned and told Xifeng to bring the Shi, Xue, and Lin girls. “And have only your Third Sister accompany them.” Xifeng assented and went over to Grandmother Jia's quarters, where she found the girls eating fruit and watching the play; Baoyu, too, had only just returned from kneeling through the sutra services at the temples. Xifeng delivered the message. The Xue sisters, Daiyu, Tanchun, and Xiangyun—the five of them—came into the garden. On meeting the guests, they duly paid their respects, exchanged greetings, and were invited to sit. Some of those present had met them before, while one or two families had not; all praised the girls in unison without cease. Xiangyun knew her best, and the Dowager Princess of Nan'an smiled at her. “You were here and heard that I had come, yet you did not come out, but waited until you were invited. Tomorrow I shall settle accounts with your uncle.” Then she took Tanchun by one hand and Baochai by the other, asked their ages, and praised them again and again. Releasing those two, she then drew Daiyu and Baoqin to her, looked them over very carefully, and praised them extravagantly too. She laughed again. “They are all delightful. You have left me quite unable to decide which one to praise.” Someone had already prepared five sets of the gifts kept in reserve: five gold rings, five jade rings, and five strings of fragrant wrist beads. The Dowager Princess of Nan'an smiled. “Do not laugh at these poor gifts, girls. Keep them to reward your maids.” The five girls hurriedly bowed their thanks. The Princess of Beijing likewise gave each of them a gift; the rest need not be recounted in detail.

p.src: During these few days, Lady You did not return to her own mansion at night. She received guests by day and slept at night in Lady Li's rooms in the garden. That evening, after attending Grandmother Jia through dinner, she heard the old lady say, “You are tired, and so am I. Go find yourselves something to eat, then turn in early. Tomorrow you must rise early for another bustling day.” Lady You assented and withdrew, then went to Xifeng's rooms to have her meal. Xifeng was upstairs supervising the storage of some new folding screens received as gifts, while only Pinger remained in the room, folding clothes with her. Lady You asked, “Has your mistress eaten yet?” Pinger replied with a smile, “If she had, surely she would have invited you.” Lady You laughed. “In that case, I shall look elsewhere for something to eat. I am so hungry I cannot bear it.” With that, she made to leave. Pinger hurriedly called after her with a smile, “Please come back, my lady. There are some pastries here. Have a little to tide you over, and eat your meal when you return.” Lady You laughed. “You are all so busy that I shall go into the garden and amuse myself with the young ladies.” She walked away even as she spoke. Unable to detain her, Pinger had to let her go.

p.src: Lady You went straight into the garden. Seeing that its main gate and various side gates were still open and that colored lanterns remained hanging everywhere, she turned and ordered a young maid to summon the women on duty. The maid went into the attendants' room but found not a soul there, so she returned and reported this to Lady You. Lady You then ordered her to summon one of the women stewards. The maid obeyed and went out to the domed pavilion beyond the second gate, where the women in charge gathered to confer and receive their assignments. When she arrived, she found only two old serving women dividing up vegetables and fruit. She asked, “Which of the ladies in charge is here? The mistress from the eastern mansion is waiting for one of them and has orders to give.” The two old women went on dividing the vegetables and fruit. Hearing that it was only the mistress from the eastern mansion, they paid little heed and replied, “The ladies in charge have only just dispersed.” The young maid said, “If they have dispersed, send word to their quarters and fetch one.” One of the old women replied, “Our only duty is to mind this room, not to carry messages. If you want someone summoned, miss, send one of the messengers.” At this, the young maid exclaimed, “Well, well! Things have certainly been turned upside down! Why will you not go and deliver the message? You might fool a newcomer with that story, but how dare you try it on me? Who but you normally carries such messages? Whenever you pick up some private bit of news, or hear that one of the ladies in charge is handing out rewards, you all fall over yourselves like eager puppies to take the message, until no one can tell who is who. If Second Mistress Lian wanted someone summoned, would you give her the same answer?” The two old women had been drinking, and the maid's exposure of their misconduct made them ashamed and furious. They retorted, “Shut your filthy mouth! Whether we deliver messages or not is none of your concern! There is no need to expose our faults. Just remember that your own parents are even better than we are at currying favor with the gentlemen in charge over there. As the saying goes, ‘When mixed noodles are dropped into clear water, I can see what you eat.’ Each household has its own gate and every family its own affairs. If you are so capable, go put on airs with the people on your side. You people have a long way to go before you can lord it over us!” The maid's face went white with anger. “Very well! Very well! Fine words indeed!” she said. She turned and went back inside to report what had happened. Lady You had already entered the garden, where she encountered Xiren, Baoqin, and Xiangyun chatting, joking, and telling stories with two nuns from the Ksitigarbha Convent. Saying that she was hungry, Lady You first went to Happy Red Court, where Xiren set out several savory and vegetarian refreshments for her. The two nuns, Baoqin, Xiangyun, and the others drank tea and continued telling stories. The young maid came straight there in search of Lady You and angrily repeated everything that had just been said. Lady You listened and said with a cold laugh, “Who are those two women?”

p.src: Hearing this, the two nuns, Baoqin, Xiangyun, and the others feared that Lady You would become angry and hurriedly tried to soothe her. “Surely nothing of the kind was said. This girl must have misheard them.” The two nuns smilingly pushed the maid away and said, “What a temper you have, child! Our lady is precious beyond price and has been worn out these past few days without so much as touching strong drink. Even our efforts to amuse her have scarcely brought half a smile to her face, so what good can come of repeating such things?” Xiren also hurriedly took the maid by the hand and led her outside, saying with a smile, “Be a good girl and go rest for a while. I shall send someone to summon them.” Lady You said, “Do not send anyone. Go yourself and bring those two old women here, then summon their Feng from the other side.” Xiren said with a smile, “I shall go and ask them to come.” Lady You replied, “You are the very person I do not want to go.” The two nuns hurriedly rose and said with a smile, “My lady, you have always been broad-minded and generous. Today is the Old Ancestress's birthday; if you lose your temper, will it not set people talking?” Baoqin and Xiangyun also joined in smilingly urging her to let the matter drop. Lady You said, “Were it not for the old lady's birthday, I would certainly not let them off. For now, we shall leave the matter where it stands.”

p.src: While they were talking, Xiren had already sent another maid to look for someone outside the garden gate. By chance the girl met Mrs Zhou Rui and told her what had happened. Although Mrs Zhou Rui held no managerial post, she had always enjoyed a certain standing as one of Lady Wang's accompanying servants. Shrewd and crafty by nature, she made a specialty of obliging and flattering every household, and so the mistresses in all the apartments liked her. On hearing this, she hurried into Happy Red Court, rushing along as she cried, “To think they should make you so angry, madam! This is outrageous! The servants in this household have been indulged beyond all bounds. Of all times, I had to be away. Had I been there, I would have slapped a few of them first and settled accounts with them after these next few days.” Seeing her, Madam You smiled and said, “Sister Zhou, since you are here, tell me who is in the right. At this late hour the gates were still wide open, the lamps and candles were blazing, and all sorts of people were coming and going. What if some unforeseen trouble occurred? p.src: Mrs Lin Zhixiao had no idea what the matter was. Lamps had already been lit, but she hurriedly took a carriage to the mansion and first sought an audience with Xifeng. By chance she met Concubine Zhao, who greeted her with a laugh: “Well, well, my dear sister! Why are you still bustling about instead of going home to rest at this hour?” Mrs Lin Zhixiao replied with a smile that she had indeed gone home, and explained how she had been summoned back. It was another instance of two sides telling the same story. Concubine Zhao was naturally fond of prying into such affairs. Moreover, she had long cultivated close relations with the women in charge, maintaining mutual connections so that they could support and cover for one another. She had already heard most of what had happened. After listening to Mrs Lin Zhixiao, she gave her a full account of the affair. Mrs Lin Zhixiao laughed and said, “So that was all! It is not worth a fart. If they are merciful, nothing more will be said; if they are less forgiving, the women will merely be beaten a few times, and that will be the end of it.” Concubine Zhao said, “My dear sister, the matter may not be serious, but it shows that they have grown far too overbearing. They went out of their way to summon you here, plainly to make sport of you and play you for a fool. Go and get some rest. You have more to do tomorrow. I shall not keep you even for tea.”

p.src: After saying this, Mrs Lin Zhixiao went out. When she reached the side gate, the daughters of the two old women came up to her, weeping and pleading for mercy. Mrs Lin Zhixiao said with a smile, “What a foolish child you are! Who told your mother to drink and talk such nonsense, stirring up trouble that even I knew nothing about? Second Mistress sent people to bind her, and even I have been blamed in the affair. How could I plead for anyone?” The two little girls were only seven or eight years old and understood nothing of such matters; they merely went on crying and pleading. Pestered beyond endurance, Mrs Lin Zhixiao said, “You foolish creatures! There is a way open to you, yet instead of taking it, you come pestering me. Mrs Lin Zhixiao spat in disgust. “You hopeless little fool! Once she goes and speaks to them, both cases will naturally be settled. They could hardly release her mother alone and beat only yours.” With that, she climbed into her carriage and left.

p.src: The little maid duly went over and told her elder sister, as well as old Mrs. Fei. Old Mrs. Fei had originally come as part of Lady Xing's dowry household and had once enjoyed considerable influence. But since the Lady Dowager had lately shown Lady Xing little favor, the people on her side had also lost much of their authority. Whenever anyone on Jia Zheng's side possessed the least standing, everyone on their side watched that person with jealous, predatory eyes. Old Mrs. Fei often presumed upon her age and Lady Xing's support. She habitually drank and vented her spleen in wild abuse and bitter complaints. Now, during so great an occasion as the Lady Dowager's birthday celebration, she could only stand by while others displayed their talents, managed affairs, shouted orders, and exercised authority. She had long felt disgruntled and made endless trouble by railing at one person under cover of abusing another and scattering spiteful remarks. The people on this side did not stoop to argue with her. When she now heard that Zhou Rui's wife had tied up her relation by marriage, it added fuel to the fire. Emboldened by drink, she pointed at the partition wall and cursed for a while, then went to plead with Lady Xing, saying that her relation had done nothing wrong: “She merely exchanged a couple of pointless words with a little maid belonging to the young mistress of the other mansion, yet Zhou Rui's wife incited our Second Mistress to have her tied up in the stables, and they mean to beat her after these next two days are over. Please, my lady—my relation is an old woman of seventy or eighty—say a word to the Second Mistress and ask her to spare the poor woman this once.” Ever since Lady Xing had been humiliated over her attempt to obtain Yuanyang, she had found the Lady Dowager increasingly cold toward her, while Xifeng enjoyed greater prestige than she did. Moreover, when the Princess Consort of Nan'an had visited the other day and asked to see the young ladies, the Lady Dowager had sent only Tanchun out to meet her, treating Yingchun as though she scarcely existed. Lady Xing had long harbored resentment and unhappiness, though she had found no way to vent them. With this pack of petty underlings constantly at her side, unable to act upon their own jealousies and grudges, they secretly fabricated rumors, stirred up trouble, and set their mistress against others. At first they merely complained about the servants on the other side, but gradually their accusations reached Xifeng herself: “She only curries favor with the Lady Dowager, and once she has won the old lady's approval, she tyrannizes over everyone, keeps Second Master Lian under her thumb, incites the Second Lady, and pays no heed at all to the rightful lady of this household.” Later they even accused Lady Wang, saying, “The old lady's dislike of you, my lady, has all been instigated by the Second Lady and Second Mistress Lian.” Even had Lady Xing possessed a heart of iron and nerves of bronze, as a woman she could hardly avoid developing feelings of estrangement; because of this, she had lately come to detest Xifeng bitterly. On hearing this lengthy complaint, she offered no opinion one way or the other. Early the next morning, after they had paid their respects to the Lady Dowager, all the clanspeople assembled, the banquet began, and the theatrical performance opened. The Lady Dowager was in high spirits. Seeing that no distant relatives were present that day and all the guests were merely younger members of her own clan, she came out in everyday clothes and ordinary adornment to receive their salutations in the hall. A single couch had been placed in the center, complete with bolster, backrest, and footstool, and she reclined upon it.

p.src: In front of, behind, and on both sides of the couch stood matching low stools, around which Baochai, Baoqin, Daiyu, Xiangyun, Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, and the other girls gathered. Jia Qiu's mother had brought her daughter Xiluan, and Jia Qiong's mother had brought her daughter Fourth Sister; together with granddaughters from several other branches of the family, there were about twenty girls, older and younger alike. The Lady Dowager was especially taken with Xiluan and Fourth Sister, both for their good looks and for the way their speech and behavior distinguished them from the others, so she called the two of them over to sit with the girls before her couch. Baoyu, meanwhile, sat at the foot of the couch massaging the Lady Dowager's legs. Aunt Xue occupied the place of honor, while the two rows below her were arranged according to family branch and seniority. Outside the curtain, the two galleries were filled with male guests of the clan, likewise seated in order. First the women guests came forward group by group to offer their salutations; only afterward did the men pay theirs. Reclining on the couch, the Lady Dowager merely had someone say, “You may dispense with the ceremony,” but by then they had already completed it. Then Lai Da and the others led the servants, who knelt in a line from the ceremonial gate all the way to the great hall and performed their kowtows. Next came the married women servants of the various households, followed by the maids of each branch; the commotion lasted as long as two or three meals. Afterward, many cages of birds were carried in and the birds were released in the central courtyard. Only after Jia She and the others had burned the ritual papers offered to Heaven, Earth, and the God of Longevity did the play and drinking begin. Not until the central intermission did the Lady Dowager go inside to rest. She told the others to do as they pleased and instructed Xifeng to keep Xiluan and Fourth Sister there for two days of amusement before sending them home. When Xifeng came out, she spoke to the girls' mothers. Both women were habitually indebted to her care and could not have wished for a more welcome invitation. The two girls also wished to play in the Garden, so by evening they did not return home. When the gathering broke up that evening, Lady Xing waited until many people were present, then smilingly interceded with Xifeng: “I heard that Second Mistress became angry last night and sent Steward Zhou's wife to tie up two old women, though I have no idea what offense they committed. Strictly speaking, I ought not to intercede. But on the old lady's auspicious birthday, when we are going out of our way to give away money and rice, assist the poor, and aid the aged, it hardly seems right for our own household to begin by tormenting people. If you will not do it for my sake, then do it for the old lady's, and let them go.” Having said this, she climbed into her carriage and left. Hearing this said before so many people, Xifeng was both humiliated and furious. For a moment she could make neither head nor tail of it; her pent-up anger turned her face purple. Turning to Lai Da's wife and the others, she forced a smile and said, “What can she mean by that? Yesterday some people from this household offended the senior young mistress of the other mansion. I feared she might take it to heart, so I left the matter entirely to her disposal; it was not because they had offended me. Who can have carried the tale so quickly?” Lady Wang asked what had happened, and Xifeng smilingly recounted the events of the previous day. You-shi also laughed and said, “Even I knew nothing about it. You really are too meddlesome.”

p.src: Xifeng said, “I waited for you to deal with them only because I did not want you to lose face. It was merely a matter of propriety. If someone in your household offended me, you would naturally send that person to me and let me do as I pleased. No matter how good a servant she might be, this rule of courtesy could not be disregarded. Whoever went over there and officiously reported it must have had nothing better to do, making such an affair out of this.” Lady Wang said, “Your mother-in-law is right. Brother Zhen’s wife is no outsider either, so there is no need for such empty ceremony. The Old Ancestress’s birthday is what matters. The proper thing is to release them.” With that, she turned and ordered someone to release the two old women. The more Xifeng thought about it, the angrier and more humiliated she became. Discouragement turned to grief, and tears rolled down her cheeks. In a fit of pique, she returned to her room to weep, taking care that no one should know. Just then, however, the Old Ancestress sent Amber to summon her at once for a conversation. Seeing her, Amber exclaimed in surprise, “Everything was fine—what has happened? They are waiting for you over there.” Hearing this, Xifeng hastily dried her tears, washed her face, reapplied her rouge and powder, and then went over with Amber. The Old Ancestress asked, “Of the households that sent gifts the other day, how many gave folding screens?” Xifeng replied, “Sixteen households sent screens altogether: twelve large ones and four small kang screens. The finest is the Jiangnan Zhen family’s large twelve-panel screen: on one side, ‘A Bed Full of Court Tablets’ woven in kesi tapestry on scarlet satin, and on the other, a ‘Hundred Longevities’ design in gold. There is also a glass screen from the family of General Wu of the Guangdong maritime command, which is fairly good.” The Old Ancestress said, “In that case, do not touch those two. Store them carefully; I intend to give them away.” Xifeng assented. Yuanyang suddenly came over and kept peering at Xifeng’s face, prompting the Old Ancestress to ask, “Do you not recognize her? What are you staring at?” Yuanyang laughed. “Her eyes look so swollen. I found it strange, and that is why I kept looking.” At this, the Old Ancestress called Xifeng closer and narrowed her eyes to examine her too. Xifeng laughed. “They suddenly began to itch, and I rubbed them until they swelled a little.” Yuanyang laughed. “You have not been upset by someone again, have you?” Xifeng said, “Who would dare upset me? Even if someone had, I would not dare cry on the Old Ancestress’s happy day.” “Quite right,” said the Old Ancestress. “I am just about to have supper. Stay here and attend me while I eat; afterward, you and Zhen’s wife may eat what remains. You two can remain here and help the two religious ladies sort the Buddha beans for me, thereby adding a little to your own longevity. Your younger sisters and Baoyu sorted some the other day; now I shall have you do it too, lest you accuse me of partiality.” As she spoke, a table of vegetarian dishes was served first.

p.src: She first went to Paddy-Sweet Cottage, but neither Li Wan nor Madam You was there. When she asked the maids, they said, “They are all at the Third Young Lady’s.” Yuanyang turned back and went to Xiaocui Hall, where, sure enough, she found everyone from the garden chatting and laughing. When they saw her, they all laughed and said, “What brings you running back here now?” Then they invited her to sit down. Yuanyang laughed. “Am I not allowed to stroll about too?” She then repeated what had just been said. Li Wan promptly rose when she heard this and ordered someone to summon one of the supervisors from each section. She told them to pass the word on to everyone. There is no need to dwell on that. Meanwhile, Madam You laughed and said, “The Old Lady really does think of everything. Even ten of us young and strong people tied together could never keep pace with her.” Li Wan said, “That girl Xifeng, relying on her uncanny cleverness, can still follow fairly close in the Old Lady’s footsteps. But we could never do it.” Yuanyang said, “Oh, enough—never mind whether she is girl Xifeng or girl Tiger; she is pitiable enough herself. Though in all these years she has never put a foot wrong before the Old Lady or Madam Wang, there is no telling how many people she has offended in private. In short, it is hard to conduct oneself properly: if you are too honest and have no resourcefulness, your parents-in-law complain that you are too simple, and the household servants do not fear you; but if you show some resourcefulness, you can hardly avoid setting one thing right at the expense of another. And our household is worse than ever now. These newly risen wives among the lower servants are each so swollen with self-satisfaction that they no longer know what they want. The least thing that displeases them, and they either wag their tongues behind people’s backs or stir up trouble here and there. I am afraid of angering the Old Lady, so I refuse to say a word about it. Otherwise, if I were to expose it all, none of us would enjoy another peaceful day. I do not say this merely because the Third Young Lady is present: when the Old Lady favors Baoyu, one can at least understand that some people grumble behind her back and call it partiality. But now that the Old Lady favors you, I hear people objecting even to that. Is that not absurd?” Tanchun laughed. “There are so many fools in the world—how could one argue with them all? I sometimes think a humble family with few members is better: though they may live plainly, they can rejoice together and everyone is happy. In a great household like ours there are so many people. Outsiders imagine that young ladies worth untold riches like us must be supremely happy, never knowing that the troubles here—too grievous even to describe—are far worse.” Baoyu said, “Not everyone frets over so many things as Third Sister does. I am always advising you about everything: pay no heed to those vulgar sayings, give no thought to mundane affairs, and simply enjoy your wealth and honored position. You are not like us, who lack such serene good fortune and are destined for the din and muddle of the world.”

p.src: Madam You said, “If only everyone were like you—truly free of every care, thinking of nothing but playing and laughing with your sisters, eating when hungry and sleeping when tired. Even in a few years you will still be just the same, without the least thought for the future.” Baoyu laughed. “So long as I can spend each day with my sisters as it comes, that is enough; when I die, it will all be over. What future is there to think about?” Li Wan and the others all laughed. “Now you are talking nonsense again. Even if you are so hopeless that you stay here until old age, do you imagine all your sisters will never marry and leave home?” Madam You laughed. “No wonder everyone says that though he grew in a human womb, he is really nothing but a simpleton and a fool.” Baoyu laughed. “Human affairs are uncertain; who knows which of us will live and which will die? If I should die today or tomorrow, this year or next, I could still say that I had lived my whole life as I wished.” Before he had finished, everyone cried, “There he goes raving again! We had better stop talking to him. Whenever we speak to him, out comes either foolish talk or madness.” Xiluan then laughed and said, “Second Brother, do not speak like that. When all the elder sisters here really have married and left, the Old Lady and Madam Wang will be lonely in any case, so I shall come and keep you company.” Li Wan, Madam You, and the others all laughed. “You too must not talk foolishly, young lady. Do you imagine you will never marry and leave home? Whom do you expect to fool with that?” Their words made Xiluan lower her head. By then the first watch had begun. Everyone returned to their own rooms to rest, and for the moment we shall say no more of any of them.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yuanyang made her way back. Just as she reached the garden entrance, she saw that the side gate stood ajar and had not yet been barred. At that hour no one was coming or going in the garden. Only the lamplight from the attendants’ quarters glimmered faintly, while a pale moon hung midway across the sky. Yuanyang had no companion with her and carried no lantern. She was alone, and her steps were so light that none of the attendants on duty noticed her. Just then she felt the need to relieve herself, so she stepped off the paved path in search of a patch of grass and came behind a rockery by the lake, beneath the shade of a great cassia tree. She had scarcely rounded the rock when she heard a sudden rustle of clothing and received a terrible fright. Peering intently, she made out two people there. At the sight of her, they tried to hide among the bushes behind the rocks. Yuanyang was sharp-eyed, and by the moonlight she clearly recognized one of them—a tall, strongly built girl in a red skirt with her hair arranged in a loose high coiffure. It was Siqi, a maid from Yingchun’s apartments. Yuanyang assumed that Siqi and another girl had also come there to relieve themselves and, on seeing her approach, had hidden merely to play a prank and frighten her. Laughing, she called, “Siqi, if you don’t come out at once, after giving me such a fright, I’ll raise the alarm and have you seized as thieves! A great girl like you, yet day or night you never seem to tire of fooling around!” Yuanyang had spoken only in jest, to make her come out. But a guilty conscience knows no peace. Siqi supposed that Yuanyang had already seen what she was up to, and feared that if she raised an alarm and everyone found out, matters would be worse still. Besides, Yuanyang had always been closer to her than the others were. So she darted out from behind the tree, seized Yuanyang by the hand, dropped to both knees, and pleaded, “Dear sister, whatever you do, please don’t make a sound!” Yuanyang, having no idea what this meant, hurriedly tried to pull her up and asked with a smile, “What is all this about?” Siqi’s whole face flushed crimson, and tears began to stream down her cheeks. Thinking back, Yuanyang realized that the other shadow had looked vaguely like a young manservant. She now guessed most of the truth, and in turn blushed to the ears with embarrassment and grew frightened herself. After composing herself for a moment, she hastily whispered, “Who is he?” Siqi knelt again and replied, “He is my cousin.” Yuanyang spat in disgust. “You wretched girl! You wretched girl!” she exclaimed. Siqi turned her head and whispered, “There’s no use hiding. Sister has already seen you. Come out quickly and kowtow to her.” Hearing this, the young manservant had no choice but to crawl out from behind the tree and knock his head on the ground over and over like a pestle pounding garlic. Yuanyang hurriedly turned to leave, but Siqi held her back and begged her bitterly, crying, “Our lives are in your hands, dear sister. Please, for mercy’s sake, spare us!” “Don’t worry,” said Yuanyang. “Whatever happens, I won’t tell a soul.” Before she had finished speaking, someone at the side gate was heard saying, “Miss Jin has gone out now. Let’s lock the side gate.”
